title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 24 (Agreements void, if considerations and objects unlawful in part)

content.overview: Section 24 provides that if any part of a single consideration for one or more objects, or any one or any part of any one of several considerations for a single object, is unlawful, the agreement is void.
content.glance: Partial unlawfulness of consideration or object in a single bargain → whole agreement void.
content.study: If any part of a single consideration for one or more objects, or any one or any part of any one of several considerations for a single object, is unlawful, the agreement is void. Section 24 prevents severing a partially unlawful single bargain so as to save the rest. Lawfulness of consideration and object is tested under s. 23. Current-law framing: identify the consideration(s) and object(s); test partial unlawfulness; conclude the whole agreement is void under s. 24.

sections.heading: Single consideration, one or more objects
sections.body: If any part of a single consideration for one or more objects is unlawful, the agreement is void.

sections.heading: Several considerations, single object
sections.body: If any one or any part of any one of several considerations for a single object is unlawful, the agreement is void.

provisions.title: Agreements void, if considerations and objects unlawful in part

examples.title: Mixed lawful and unlawful consideration
examples.body: A single consideration partly for a lawful object and partly for an unlawful object — the agreement is void under s. 24.

hypotheticals.question: Can the lawful part of a single mixed bargain be saved?
hypotheticals.analysis: Under s. 24, if any part of the single consideration or any of several considerations for a single object is unlawful, the agreement is void.

distinctions.title: Scope of s-24
distinctions.body: Applies only within the elements and consequences stated in the statutory text.

misconceptions.trap: Courts always sever the unlawful part and enforce the rest.
misconceptions.correction: Section 24 voids the agreement when consideration or object is unlawful in part in the ways specified.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 24 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify consideration(s) and object(s). II. Test partial unlawfulness under s. 23. III. Apply s. 24 voidness. IV. Conclude.
